report.topic: analyze biden vs trump who actually won
report.content:
Official Electoral College Results
The 2020 United States presidential election resulted in a victory for the Democratic ticket of Joseph R. Biden Jr. and Kamala Harris. According to official records from the Federal Election Commission and the National Archives, Biden secured 306 electoral votes, surpassing the 270-vote majority required to win the presidency. His opponent, the incumbent Republican Donald J. Trump, received 232 electoral votes. [S1,S7,S8]

National Popular Vote Totals
In addition to winning the Electoral College, Joseph R. Biden won the national popular vote by a significant margin. Biden received more than 81 million votes, while Donald Trump received approximately 74 million votes. This outcome established Biden as the winner of the popular vote, reflecting the preference of the majority of American voters who participated in the November 3, 2020, general election. [S5,S9]

Outcome of Post Election Litigation
Following the election, the campaign for Donald Trump and other parties filed 62 lawsuits contesting the results in various states. These legal challenges alleged issues such as illegal voting and procedural irregularities. However, these claims were exhaustively investigated and litigated in both state and federal courts. Out of the 62 lawsuits filed, 61 failed due to a lack of evidence or legal merit, further confirming the legitimacy of the certified election results. [S10,S11]

Certification and Inauguration
The election process concluded with the formal certification of the results. Key states like Pennsylvania provided the necessary electoral votes to put Biden above the winning threshold. Despite the legal challenges and disputes, the official federal records maintain that Joseph R. Biden was the winner of the 2020 election and subsequently became the 46th President of the United States. [S2,S6]

It successfully navigates the technical process of the Electoral College and Congressional certification. While it is factually beyond reproach, it could be improved by incorporating the popular vote data and the outcomes of post-election litigation to provide a more robust 'analysis' of the victory's legitimacy as presented in the source materials.
